findings.title: Revalidate planned fixes after committed checkout changes
findings.description: The apply-time readiness check detects uncommitted edits but not changes committed while confirmation is pending. A reordered plan can therefore pass readiness with a clean tree, after which `applyFixes` uses stale line indices. The inspected checkbox writer only checks for checkbox syntax, so it can update—and automatically commit—the wrong entry. Record and verify the planning revision/content before applying; add a regression test that commits reordered entries between planning and application.

findings.title: Commit timeouts can incorrectly report committed fixes as deferred
findings.description: A commit can update HEAD before a slow post-commit hook causes the git subprocess to time out. This catch treats every failure as an unsuccessful commit and restores paths from the current HEAD, which already contains the fixes. It then clears successful fix logs and reports `COMMIT_FAILED`, despite the changes remaining committed. Capture HEAD before committing and reconcile it after failure before deciding whether rollback or deferral is appropriate. Add coverage for a timeout after HEAD advances.
